triggers.grounds: Well calibrated; the band is honest and if anything conservative. Both edges rest on ruled tier-1 vocative openers standing in the cited verses' own bytes: Prov.1.8 opens שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי (oshb:Prov.1.8, words 1-2, byte tier) and the following unit opens בְּנִ֡י אִם (oshb:Prov.1.10, words 1-2, byte tier), a second vocative carrying its own conditional, so the back edge is a text seam and not a convenience cut. The front edge is corroborated at tier-3 by the PE at Prov.1.7 (pmarks_Prov.json marks Prov.1.7 = PE; 51 PE + 1 SAMEKH book-wide, single-witness, disclosed as such in the refs). The stated reason for the low band is byte-checkable and true: at 2 verses the unit sits below the 4-8 verse range the C1 lecture rows run to, and the genuinely unresolved question - whether Prov.1.8-Prov.1.9 is a unit or the head of the Prov.1.8-Prov.1.19 lecture the row itself names as its rival - is settled by no byte signal, the parashah layer being silent between the PE at Prov.1.7 and the PE at Prov.1.19. No low-band label is masking a defective warrant here.

findings.claim: A paseq seg stands in the row's own closing verse and is nowhere disclosed.
findings.grounds: pmarks_Prov.json paseq records 1 seg at Prov.1.9 (60 segs / 57 verses book-wide; count-only, no offsets; single-witness). Prov.1.9 is this row's span end, yet the row names no paseq in any field and its boundary_evidence_refs carry only oshb:Prov.1.7 (petuchah, single-witness), web:Prov.1.10 and web:Prov.1.19. The book's standing rule extends symmetry completion to 'every other disclosure object', not just the parashah layer, and the corpus applies it that way at the Prov.3.27-Prov.3.31 row, which discloses the Prov.3.28 paseq inline alongside its K/Q notes. The Tier-0 symmetry gate reaches only the PE/SAMEKH inventory (check_marks rule 2 iterates the marks inventory alone), so this gap passes check_marks GREEN and is model territory. Nothing about the seam changes: the paseq is a seg-layer object absent from the staged verse bytes and carries no boundary weight.
findings.proposed_change: Disclosure repair only: add an oshb:Prov.1.9 (paseq, single-witness) entry to boundary_evidence_refs and a count-only mention in device_notes, with no intra-verse position claim (the inventory records none).

triggers.grounds: Pure disclosure, and the disclosure cuts against the row's own conclusion rather than propping it up - the tier-4 fact does neither driver nor corroboration work. The fact is byte-true: verse_map_web.json text for Prov.1.22 opens with U+201C at index 0 while Prov.1.20 and Prov.1.21 carry no quotation mark at all, so WEB does open its own curly quotation mark at 1:22. The row's sentence reads it expressly as 'an editorial signal (Tier-4-adjacent) rather than a Hebrew person-shift' - i.e. it neutralises a mark that, if credited, would have SUPPORTED the rival split at 1:22 that the row rejects. The seam rests elsewhere: the subject/speaker change at Prov.1.20 plus PE at Prov.1.19 and PE at Prov.1.33 (pmarks marks, both PE, tier-3 weak, single-witness, disclosed), and the rival is rejected on a tier-1 ground ('a shift in grammatical person alone, without a fresh tier-1 speech-frame marker'). The Hebrew claim the sentence carries is also byte-true: oshb:Prov.1.22 carries no first-person form, while oshb:Prov.1.23 carries five (my reproof, I will pour out, my spirit, I will make known, my words), and both witnesses agree. Quotation handling inside the quoted runs is verbatim, not degraded: verse_map_web.json clean for Prov.1.22 and Prov.1.33 carries U+0022 at exactly the indices where text carries U+201C / U+201D, so the row's straight-quote rendering reproduces the staged clean layer exactly (check_web_quotes GREEN, 7 quotes; the web:Prov.1.23 run is verbatim against clean, the raw text there differing only by an inline WEB footnote, which is tier-4 apparatus).

findings.claim: Two paseq segs inside the span go undisclosed while the K/Q in the same span is disclosed.
findings.grounds: pmarks_Prov.json paseq records 1 seg each at Prov.1.22 and Prov.1.27, both inside the span Prov.1.20-Prov.1.33 (book-wide 60 segs / 57 verses; count-only; single-witness). The row discloses the Prov.1.27 ketiv/qere properly - the refs carry oshb:Prov.1.27 (ketiv/qere, single-witness) and the 'storm-word' attribution is itself byte-verifiable, since oshb:Prov.1.27 carries the unpointed inline ketiv token immediately before its pointed qere - but names no paseq anywhere, and Prov.1.22 is the very verse the boundary_rationale argues at length. The asymmetry is the defect, not the seam: paseq is a seg-layer object absent from the staged verse bytes and never a boundary signal. Invisible to Tier-0 (check_marks GREEN; its symmetry arm iterates only the PE/SAMEKH inventory).
findings.proposed_change: Disclosure repair only: add oshb:Prov.1.22 (paseq, single-witness) and extend the existing Prov.1.27 entry to oshb:Prov.1.27 (ketiv/qere, single-witness; paseq, single-witness), matching the formula already used at the Prov.3.27-Prov.3.31 row; count-only, no position claim.

triggers.grounds: Correctly calibrated at the book's own ceiling and byte-sound throughout. The span is the whole of chapter 2, so the chapter-fallback rule caps confidence at medium_low; the row sits exactly at the cap and does not reach past it. Re-derived from bytes: the chapter's single vocative at Prov.2.1 matches prov_device_inventory.json bni_address by_chapter '2': 1 (count object = verses carrying the word-bound vocative at any position), and the row ships the digit ('occurring once across its 22 verses'); the twin-apodosis claim is byte-identical as stated - word 1 of oshb:Prov.2.5, אָ֗ז, and word 1 of oshb:Prov.2.9 are the same four codepoints - as is the twin infinitive, word 1 of oshb:Prov.2.12, לְ֭הַצִּ֣ילְךָ, equalling word 1 of oshb:Prov.2.16 across fourteen codepoints; the three protases plus one purpose-infinitive are visible in the openers of oshb:Prov.2.1, oshb:Prov.2.3 and oshb:Prov.2.4 against the infinitive opening oshb:Prov.2.2; PE at Prov.1.33, PE at Prov.2.22 and the K/Q notes at Prov.2.7 and Prov.2.8 all match pmarks_Prov.json under the claimed types, single-witness disclosed; chapter 2 carries no paseq, so the row's silence there is complete rather than a gap; and the web:Prov.2.22 run is verbatim. The stated reason for the low band is honest and names its cost - the finer strophic split 'is textually real' and is set aside for the chapter's single-sentence grammar - with frontier_flag_considered true. The one-word gloss 'therefore' at oshb:Prov.2.20 is not an overreach either: WEB renders that verse “Therefore walk in the way of good men, and keep the paths of the righteous.” (web:Prov.2.20).

Both arms fail. TEST 2: the reference carries a scoped count claim, and re-derived from the inventory it names the digit is wrong - five bni_address verses stand inside Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27, not four. Recorded as the medium finding below.

findings.class: E-05 count-object / scoped digit (with E-06 register)
findings.claim: The row's part-scoped vocative digit misreports the very inventory it cites: the range holds five bni_address verses, not four.
findings.grounds: prov_device_inventory.json bni_address declares count_object 'verses containing the word-bound VOCATIVE token beni (my son; chirik), any position, pointed tier (E-1 corrected)', count 22, by_chapter 3:3 and 4:2; its refs inside Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 are Prov.3.1, Prov.3.11, Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 - FIVE. My independent sweep agrees: over consonantal_index.json, the word-bound skeleton בני returns 30 verses / 30 tokens book-wide, of which 22 carry the chirik vocative (both attested spellings, with and without dagesh in the bet: 19 + 3) and 8 the tsere construct, i.e. exactly the inventory's 22, one token per verse - so the row's '22 tokens book-wide' happens to coincide numerically while naming the wrong unit (the inventory counts verses). The omitted verse is Prov.3.11, where the vocative stands as word 3, מוּסַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה בְּנִ֣י (oshb:Prov.3.11, words 1-3, byte tier); it drops out only under a verse-initial-opening count object, which the row never names while citing an any-position inventory. Not load-bearing for the seam: word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.1 is בְּ֭נִי at byte tier and the row closes on the PE at Prov.3.4 (pmarks, PE, tier-3 weak, single-witness), both independently verified, and the divine-name contrast the row draws is byte-true (no word-bound YHWH token anywhere in Prov.3.1-Prov.3.4; five across Prov.3.5-Prov.3.12).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, text register, count object named and digit re-derived - e.g. 'the vocative opens Prov.3.1 and recurs verse-initially at Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 (word-bound vocative verses across Prov.3-4: 5, the fifth at Prov.3.11 standing mid-verse; 22 verses book-wide)'; drop 'the part' and the inventory name from row prose.

findings.claim: The rival narrower cut is rejected first on the ABSENCE of a parashah/disclosure object, an inference the book's mark law forbids.
findings.grounds: The strongest_rejected_alternative reads that a cut after 3.24 'lacks any parashah or disclosure-object support, and both halves keep the same second-person, self-directed object, so the wider bound is kept instead'. The absence is byte-true - pmarks_Prov.json carries PE at Prov.3.18 and PE at Prov.3.35 with nothing between, and neither paseq nor K/Q anywhere in Prov.3.21-Prov.3.26 - but pmarks_Prov.json marks_note states in terms 'Absence is NEVER counterevidence', and the book strategy repeats it for the Writings parashah layer, so the first of the two grounds offered against the rival is inadmissible. It is not alone load-bearing: the second ground (both halves keep the same second-person, self-directed object) is positive and textual and stands on its own, and the row's own edges are untouched - the vocative בְּ֭נִי at oshb:Prov.3.21 (word 1, byte tier) and the object shift at Prov.3.27. Note the contrast within the same row: the in-span statement 'No petuchah or other disclosure-object note falls inside this span' is proper disclosure and is byte-true; only its conversion into a reason against the rival is the defect.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: rest the rival's rejection on the positive ground alone (the shared second-person, self-directed object across 3.21-3.24 and 3.25-3.26) and delete the 'lacks any parashah or disclosure-object support' clause; keep the in-span absence statement where it stands, as disclosure.

triggers.grounds: Honest and byte-anchored. The back seam is genuinely the weak one and the row says exactly why: the quoted paternal instruction opens inside Prov.4.4 with וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֗י (oshb:Prov.4.4, words 2-3, byte tier) and runs on past the row's edge, so the seam rests on a speech-frame device with no corroboration available - pmarks_Prov.json carries no mark, no paseq and no K/Q anywhere in Prov.4.1-Prov.4.4 (nearest are the PE at Prov.3.35, correctly disclosed as the previous unit's, and the K/Q at Prov.4.16), precisely as the row states. The front seam is strong and byte-true: שִׁמְע֣וּ בָ֭נִים (oshb:Prov.4.1, words 1-2, byte tier) is a plural address against the singular vocative of the neighbouring openers. The straddling quotation is disclosed on both sides of the seam, the following row recording that its opening 'inherits the reported-speech frame established in 4.4, outside its own span', which satisfies the cross-seam cohesion rule. medium_low with frontier_flag_considered true is the right band; nothing defective is hiding under it.

findings.class: E-05 digit / E-18 cross-row claim in workflow register
findings.claim: '3 of 4 lecture-openers in this part (3.1, 3.21, 4.10, 4.20)' is arithmetically false against its own list: all four carry the singular vocative.
findings.grounds: Every verse the row lists is a bni_address ref in prov_device_inventory.json and the singular vocative is byte-present in each: word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.1 is בְּ֭נִי, word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.21 is בְּ֭נִי, words 1-2 of oshb:Prov.4.10 are שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי and word 1 of oshb:Prov.4.20 is בְּ֭נִי - all at byte tier, so the ratio is 4 of 4. Read the other way, as four openers out of a set that also contains this row's own plural opener at Prov.4.1, it would be 4 of 5; on neither reading is the shipped digit right, and the row never names the count object that would decide it (verse-initial opener vs the inventory's any-position vocative verse, of which Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 holds five, Prov.3.11 included). The seam does not depend on the digit: the contrast the row actually needs is the plural שִׁמְע֣וּ בָ֭נִים (oshb:Prov.4.1, words 1-2, byte tier) against those singular openers, and that is byte-true whatever the tally.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair in text register with the object named: e.g. 'a plural address, against the singular vocative opening Prov.3.1, Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 (4 of 4 verse-initial openers across Prov.3-4)'; remove 'in this part' from boundary_rationale and the row-set reference from device_notes.

triggers.grounds: Well calibrated, and unusually precise in what it does assert. The front edge inherits the reported-speech frame opened inside Prov.4.4, outside the row's own span, and the row discloses exactly that; pmarks_Prov.json confirms the row's 'No disclosure object falls inside this span' - no mark, no paseq and no K/Q anywhere in Prov.4.5-Prov.4.9. The 4:7 anatomy re-collates exactly as written: oshb:Prov.4.7 has eight words and the row's three splices land at words 3-4, words 5-6 and words 7-8, each at byte tier, while the imperative pair of oshb:Prov.4.5 (words 1-4) collates at only accent_stripped and skeleton tiers against 4:7's copies - so 'echoed' and 'split' are right and no byte-identity is claimed between the two verses. The medium_low band prices the unmarked, quotation-internal front seam honestly, with frontier_flag_considered true; the back seam at the Prov.4.10 vocative is the strong one.
